newsitem.title: CANADA: New Gallup Canada poll shows growing Liberal lead.
newsitem.headline: New Gallup Canada poll shows growing Liberal lead.

text.p: A new poll released on Friday showed the lead of Canada's ruling Liberals widening as they head into an election, which is expected on June 2.
The Gallup Canada survey showed Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberals with the support of 55 percent of decided voters, 40 points ahead of their nearest rival.
It put the Conservatives at 15 percent, the separatist Bloc Quebecois at 11 percent, Reform at 10 percent and the New Democratic Party (NDP) at nine percent.

"Jean Chretien's federal Liberals continue to hold a comfortable lead in the hearts and minds of Canadian voters," the polling organization said, adding that another majority government was assured if the numbers held.
But 35 percent of Canadian voters remained undecided.
The poll covered 1,006 adults from April 10-16. A Gallup survey a month earlier had the Liberals at 52 percent, Conservatives 18, Bloc 10, Reform nine and NDP nine.

A government official said on Friday that Chretien would call a June 2 election on Sunday, 17 months before he was required to do so. The Liberals won in 1993 with 41 percent to Reform's 19 percent, the Conservatives' 16 and the Bloc's 14.
The poll carries a margin of error of 3.1 percentage points 19 times out of 20.

In contrast to an Angus Reid poll published on April 3, Gallup also put the Liberals ahead in every region -- 60-27 percent over Reform in British Columbia and 44-23 ahead in the Prairies; 47-44 ahead of the Bloc in Quebec; and 63-20 ahead of the Conservatives and ahead 53-32 in the Atlantic.
The April 3 poll put the Bloc ahead in Quebec and Reform ahead in British Columbia and Alberta.
